draft.title: Why we have seasons
card: The Earth spins on an axis, an imaginary line through the North and South Poles. The axis is tilted. It always points the same way in space as the Earth travels around the sun once a year.
the hemisphere tilted towards the sun gets more direct, concentrated sunlight and longer days. Both of these make it warmer.
the hemisphere tilted away from the sun gets less direct, more spread out sunlight and shorter days. Both of these make it cooler.
The two hemispheres take turns through the year, so when it is summer in Australia it is winter in the northern hemisphere.
draft.remember: The tilt means each hemisphere takes turns facing the sun more directly.

a.q: Why is it summer in Perth when the southern hemisphere is tilted towards the sun?
opts: The sunlight is more concentrated and the days are longer
The Earth is closer to the sun than at any other time
The Earth spins faster, so it gets more sunlight in total
The sun gives off more heat during the southern summer
a.why: A tilt towards the sun means more direct, concentrated light and longer days, which warm the land. The distance to the sun is not the cause: the seasons come from the tilt of the axis.
a.clue: Think about how the light lands and how long the day is.

b.q: Mei lives in Hobart. She says it is December there and her cousin in Canada is wearing a heavy coat. What best explains this?
opts: Each hemisphere is tilted towards the sun at opposite times
Canada is always further from the sun than Tasmania is
The Earth's axis tilts back and forth during each month
The sun only shines on one hemisphere at a time
b.why: In December the southern hemisphere is tilted towards the sun, so Hobart has summer. The northern hemisphere is tilted away, so Canada has winter. Distance is not the reason, because the Earth's tilt makes the hemispheres swap places through the year.
b.clue: When one hemisphere tilts towards the sun, what does the other do?

a.best: The sunlight is more concentrated and the days are longer

b.best: Each hemisphere is tilted towards the sun at opposite times

problems.detail: The clue ('how the light lands and how long the day is') maps directly onto the right option's two parts (concentrated light, longer days), so a student can match words without understanding the idea.

The distractor 'The Earth is closer to the sun than at any other time' is nearly true for the southern summer, because Earth's closest approach to the sun (perihelion) is in early January. It is wrong only as the reason for summer, so a careful student who knows this may be confused. A distractor that is plainly false, or a stem that clearly asks for the cause, would be safer.

the hemisphere tilted towards the sun gets more direct sunlight, so the same light falls on a smaller area and is more concentrated. Its days are also longer. Both of these make it warmer.
the hemisphere tilted away from the sun gets less direct, more spread out sunlight and shorter days. Both of these make it cooler.
The two hemispheres take turns through the year, so when it is summer in Australia it is winter in the northern hemisphere. Seasons are caused by the tilt, not by the Earth's distance from the sun.
